correctness.rationale: For each positive trajectory define the nonnegative recession clock Phi_h; derivative is -1 exactly above threshold. Summing its jumps telescopes to total exceedance time. Each later impulse of size P yields at most Phi_h(h+P), with equality iff its pre-pulse state equals h, because 1/f is strictly decreasing. First increment equals Phi_h(Pfirst). The bound is simultaneously attained by strictly positive threshold-return gaps. Optimizing over first pulse uses strictly increasing H(P)=-int_P^{P+h} 1/f, forcing any largest increment first; all and only the stated maximizing schedules result. All edge cases P_i>h, n>=2, positive Lipschitz strictly increasing f and final decay handled explicitly. Independent exact-rational checker passed 36006 assertions for f=q and f=q^2; general proof is analytic.

value.rationale: The duration above a damaging river-flow level is a hydrologically motivated risk objective independent of the event peak. The theorem optimizes a genuinely combinatorial calendar of any number of heterogeneous storm increments, gives complete equality characterization under every strictly increasing recession law without convexity or linearity, and identifies the nonobvious largest-first and threshold-touch optimal timing. It supplies a sharp worst-case hazard-duration upper bound from pulse magnitudes and the recession relation. Limits on instant pulses, fixed threshold and no finite horizon are explicit; the claim is not a field forecast.
